title: A full stop or semicolon closes the current row
defect: On the first held-out run (seed 20260601) 'X. after Y, Z', 'X; before Y, Z' and 'X. if C, Z' were mis-parsed: '.' and ';' were CLOSE tokens that do not end a row, so a following after/before/if/unless attached to X as an infix connector or suffix condition. Trace: at the token 'after', boundary unit bnd_AFTER fired (row 0 has an action) and set reverse=1; the intended reading needs the row to be closed already.
hypothesis: The network lacks a 'sentence ended' transition. If '.' and ';' behave like the sequence connectors (advance the pointer when the row has an action) but a row opened only by a full stop is not counted as a dangling connector, then prefix after/before/if clauses after a full stop are parsed as new clauses and a trailing full stop is still accepted.
affected: token feature STOP (new); row field OPEN (new, marker); A units bnd_STOP, bnd_STOP_pb; B units w_OPEN, w_CCL_stop; E rows '.' and ';'; tensor tf_w (TIME -> OPEN).
mathematical_effect: bnd_STOP = relu(x_STOP + hasACT - PB - 1) is the same AND gadget as bnd_SEQ, so STOP advances the pointer p <- S p when the row holds an action. OPEN is written by relu(adv - x_STOP): it is 1 on rows opened by a connector other than STOP. The dangling-row detector reads OPEN instead of TIME, so a row opened by '.' and left empty contributes 0 error, while 'then' at the end still contributes 1.
expected: Targets (tests/next/defects-001.jsonl) become exact matches; dev set unchanged; 'move X left then' still rejected; trailing '.' still accepted.
